facts.fact: Rod Whitman, Dave Axland and Keith Cutten; opened 2 May 2024; 19 par 3s.
Named for Shorty Dow, caretaker of the land that became the resort. The 6th and 18th share a horseshoe-shaped double green.

current.subject: A spotted fawn standing in dune grass (developer's request).
current.keep: The fawn: small, young, a short course.
current.weaknesses: Thin legs and a standing pose make a spindly silhouette at 1x.

concepts.name: The Bedded Fawn
concepts.rationale: The fawn lies curled in the dune grass, head up and ears wide: one compact, round silhouette full of spots.
concepts.symbolism: Young and small and at home in the dunes, like a par-3 course.
concepts.strengths: Much stronger shape than the standing fawn; charming.

concepts.name: The Horseshoe
concepts.rationale: The 6th/18th double green seen from above: a horseshoe of putting surface with a pin at each end, in the dunes.
concepts.symbolism: Luck and two pins on one green: the fun of a par-3 course.
concepts.typography: Rye, a frontier display face, for the caretaker who called himself sheriff.
concepts.tradeoffs: Without the story it could read as a green magnet.

recommendation: Concept 1. The bedded fawn is the developer's subject done right; the Horseshoe is a great secondary mark.
